sentences.text: Kinnareemimus is known from very incomplete remains including vertebrae, parts of the pubic bones, metatarsals, and an incomplete fibula.
Later estimates suggest Kinnareemimus was about 1.8 meters long and weighed approximately 13 kilograms.
Kinnareemimus is distinguished by a semi-arctometatarsalian condition where the third metatarsal remains visible from the front and narrows before flaring into a triangular shape at the tip.
In 2024, the diagnosis was updated to include ventrally flattened toe claws with flexor fossae, reinforcing its classification within ornithomimosaurs.
The genus name Kinnareemimus refers to the kinnara, a creature from Hindu mythology represented in Thailand with a female body and bird legs, alluding to the animal's bird-like feet.
Kinnareemimus may be the oldest known ornithomimosaur, depending on the age of the Sao Khua Formation.
The species name khonkaenensis honors Khon Kaen Province in northeastern Thailand, where the fossils were found.
Kinnareemimus was formally described in 2009 by Eric Buffetaut, Varavudh Suteethorn, and Haiyan Tong.
The name Kinnareemimus was first mentioned in a 1999 work by Sasithorn Kamsupha and as Ginnareemimus in a 2000 publication by Ryuichi Kaneko.
The genus Kinnareemimus was named by Buffetaut and colleagues in 2009.
Evidence of unfused sutures suggests that at least some of the preserved vertebrae came from a juvenile individual.
Varying degrees of fusion in the preserved tail vertebrae indicate the fossils represent individuals of different ages.
Multiple metatarsal bones from different individuals allow for a reasonably precise reconstruction of the foot structure.

The estimated tarsus length in Kinnareemimus was comparable to Garudimimus but substantially smaller than the ratios seen in Struthiomimus and Gallimimus, which are believed to be well-adapted for running.
Kinnareemimus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately between 125 and 120 million years ago.
Kinnareemimus lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 135 to 130 million years ago, from the Valanginian to the Hauterivian.
Kinnareemimus lived in what is now Asia.
The remains of Kinnareemimus were found in Thailand.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Kinnareemimus as the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
The Sao Khua Formation, where Kinnareemimus fossils were found, consists of sediments indicating a fluvial environment with lakes, floodplains, and braided channels.
Recent analyses have found very little support for classifying Kinnareemimus as an ornithomimosaur in major phylogenetic studies.
There is significant debate regarding the classification of Kinnareemimus, with studies suggesting it could be a basal coelurosaur, a tyrannosauroid, or an alvarezsauroid.
